contract.goal: Add truncate, slugify and wordCount helpers to the textkit library, each with its own test file, plus a bin/textkit.js command-line script that runs any of them by name, and document everything in the README.
outOfScope: Changing or removing the existing capitalize helper or its test
Adding dependencies, a build step, a linter or a different test runner
Unicode-aware slugging (accent stripping, punctuation removal, non-Latin scripts)
Adding a package.json bin field, publishing, or changing the version
CLI features beyond running the three helpers by name (flags, help text, interactive mode, other helpers)
Exact CLI error messages or exit codes for bad input

criteria.text: truncate(text, max) is exported from src/index.js. When text is longer than max, it returns a string of at most max characters that ends with exactly one '…' (U+2026) and keeps the start of the text. When text already fits within max, it is returned unchanged.

proof.run: node --input-type=module -e "import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { truncate } from './src/index.js'; for (const m of [1,2,5,8]) { const r = truncate('hello world', m); assert.ok(r.length <= m, 'too long for '+m); assert.ok(r.endsWith('…') && !r.endsWith('……'), 'ellipsis for '+m); assert.equal(r.split('…').length, 2, 'single ellipsis for '+m); } assert.ok(truncate('hello world', 8).startsWith('hello')); assert.equal(truncate('hi', 8), 'hi'); assert.equal(truncate('hello', 5), 'hello');"

criteria.text: slugify(text) is exported from src/index.js. It lower-cases the text and joins whitespace-separated words with single dashes, with no leading or trailing dash, even when the input has repeated or surrounding whitespace.

proof.run: node --input-type=module -e "import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { slugify } from './src/index.js'; assert.equal(slugify('Hello World'), 'hello-world'); assert.equal(slugify('  Foo   Bar \t baz  '), 'foo-bar-baz'); assert.equal(slugify('Single'), 'single');"

criteria.text: wordCount(text) is exported from src/index.js. It returns the number of words separated by whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines), ignoring leading, trailing and repeated whitespace, and returns 0 for an empty or whitespace-only string.

proof.run: node --input-type=module -e "import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { wordCount } from './src/index.js'; assert.equal(wordCount('a b  c'), 3); assert.equal(wordCount(' a\tb\nc '), 3); assert.equal(wordCount('one'), 1); assert.equal(wordCount(''), 0); assert.equal(wordCount('   '), 0);"

test/slugify.test.js exists, contains at least one test, and passes.
test/wordCount.test.js exists, contains at least one test, and passes.

Running `node bin/textkit.js <name> <text> [max]` with name truncate, slugify or wordCount prints the result of that helper to stdout and exits 0. For truncate the second argument is the text and the third is max.

proof.run: node --input-type=module -e "import assert from 'node:assert/strict'; import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'; const run = (...a) => execFileSync('node', ['bin/textkit.js', ...a], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim(); assert.equal(run('slugify', 'Hello   World'), 'hello-world'); assert.equal(run('wordCount', 'a b  c'), '3'); const t = run('truncate', 'hello world', '8'); assert.ok(t.length <= 8 && t.endsWith('…') && t.startsWith('hello'));"

tasks.title: Add truncate, slugify, wordCount helpers with tests
tasks.brief: Repo is an ES module project (package.json type=module, tests run with node --test, no deps). src/index.js currently exports only capitalize; leave it and test/capitalize.test.js untouched. Add and export from src/index.js: truncate(text, max): if text.length <= max return text unchanged; otherwise return text.slice(0, max-1) + '…' (U+2026), so the result is at most max chars with exactly one ellipsis (handle max=1 -> '…'; max<1 may return '…' or ''). slugify(text): trim, lower-case, split on /\s+/ and join with '-' (empty/whitespace-only input -> ''). wordCount(text): trim; return 0 if empty, else split on /\s+/ and return the length. Add test/truncate.test.js, test/slugify.test.js, test/wordCount.test.js using node:test and node:assert/strict, importing from ../src/index.js, each with at least one passing test (cover fit/no-fit, repeated/surrounding whitespace, empty input, etc.). Verify with node --test.

tasks.title: Add bin/textkit.js CLI
tasks.brief: Create bin/textkit.js (ES module, add a '#!/usr/bin/env node' shebang). It must import { truncate, slugify, wordCount } from '../src/index.js' and call them; do not re-implement any logic. Usage: node bin/textkit.js <name> <text> [max]. name is one of truncate, slugify, wordCount; look it up in a map of the imported functions. For truncate call truncate(text, Number(max)). Print the result with console.log to stdout and exit 0. Unknown name or bad input: print something to stderr and exit non-zero (exact message unimportant). No flags, help, or other features. Do not touch src/index.js, tests or README. Verify e.g. node bin/textkit.js slugify 'Hello   World' prints hello-world.

T1.title: Add truncate, slugify, wordCount helpers with tests
T1.summary: I added truncate, slugify and wordCount to src/index.js, along with test/truncate.test.js, test/slugify.test.js and test/wordCount.test.js. `node --test` passes all 8 tests, including the existing capitalize test, which I left untouched. I also ran a truncate check like the C1 proof (lengths for max 1, 2, 5 and 8, a single ellipsis, text starting with 'hello'), and it passed. I didn't run the C2 and C3 proof commands as written. The tests I wrote assert the same cases. The work is committed.
T1.notes: All three helpers are named exports of src/index.js. truncate(text, max) returns the text unchanged if it fits. If it doesn't, it returns text.slice(0, max-1) + '…', and for max<1 it returns '…'. For example, truncate('hello world', 8) is 'hello w…'. slugify('  Foo   Bar \t baz  ') is 'foo-bar-baz', and slugify('') is ''. wordCount(' a\tb\nc ') is 3, and wordCount('') is 0. The CLI task must convert max with Number(argv[4]) before calling truncate, because argv values are strings.

T2.title: Add bin/textkit.js CLI
T2.summary: Added bin/textkit.js, an ES module with a node shebang. It imports truncate, slugify and wordCount from ../src/index.js and looks the name up in a map. truncate gets Number(max). The result goes to stdout with exit 0. An unknown name, missing text or a non-numeric max for truncate prints to stderr and exits 1. The C7 proof command passes, and I checked that an unknown name exits 1. I did not run `node --test`.
T2.notes: Usage: `node bin/textkit.js <truncate|slugify|wordCount> <text> [max]`. The file is committed and executable. For the README, `node bin/textkit.js slugify 'Hello   World'` prints `hello-world`, and `node bin/textkit.js truncate 'hello world' 8` prints `hello w…`. The second example comes from T1's note, so I didn't run it separately.
